questions.statement: Choose the sentence in the present simple: 'My father ____ to Lima every year for the Fair.'
questions.context: Practica de presente simple, Lima, grado 11.

options.feedback: The base form is used with I, you, we and they.
Third person singular takes -s in the present simple.
An auxiliary and a bare verb cannot be combined this way.
The gerund alone cannot function as the verb of the clause.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto 'my father' es tercera persona singular, por eso el verbo lleva -s. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present simple correctly with a time expression?

options.text: The market is opening every Sunday at six.
options.feedback: The present continuous with 'every' describes a temporary arrangement.

options.text: The market opened every Sunday at six.
options.feedback: The simple past is incompatible with a habit that still holds.

options.text: The market opens every Sunday at six.
options.feedback: 'Every Sunday' marks a recurring habit, so the present simple is required.

options.text: The market will open every Sunday at six.
options.feedback: 'Will' points to the future, not to a standing schedule.

questions.explanation:
'Every' introduce una accion habitual y por eso exige el presente simple. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

options.text: He do not need a visa for that trip.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must agree with 'he', which is 'does'.

options.text: He does not need a visa for that trip.
options.feedback: 'Does not' plus base verb is the correct negative structure.

options.text: He not needs a visa for that trip.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must precede the adverb 'not'.

options.text: He does not needs a visa for that trip.
options.feedback: After 'does not' the verb returns to the base form 'need'.

La negacion requiere 'does not' seguido del verbo en forma base cuando el sujeto es singular de tercera persona.

options.text: The Amazon river flowing through two countries.
options.feedback: There is no finite verb: 'flowing' cannot close the clause.

options.text: It indicates an action in progress
options.feedback: That is the function of 'at the moment' with the continuous form.

options.text: It indicates a permanent habit, which fits the present simple
options.feedback: Frequency adverbs of this kind normally accompany the simple present.

options.text: It indicates a finished past action
options.feedback: Frequency adverbs do not fix a past time.
